claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi is a high-entropy alloy system suitable as the proposed baseline composition.
HEA intermediate layers are currently used in plasma-facing reactor components.
The baseline HEA intermediate layer is predominantly FCC and/or BCC.
The baseline intermediate layer has acceptable mechanical strength and microstructural stability.
The baseline intermediate layer has limited heat-transfer efficiency.
Adding approximately 5 at% Cu to the baseline HEA will improve its effective thermal conductivity.
Adding approximately 5 at% Cu will preserve sufficient structural integrity.
Approximately 700–1000 °C and cyclic thermal loading are representative service conditions for plasma-facing intermediate layers.
The added Cu will be uniformly dispersed in a homogeneous microstructure without significant phase segregation.
Approximately 5 at% Cu will not cause significant grain-boundary embrittlement.
Copper possesses high intrinsic thermal conductivity.
Dispersed Cu at approximately 5 at% will form interconnected conductive channels in the HEA.
The proposed Cu-rich channels will enhance both electron and phonon transport.
The remaining multiphase HEA structure will retain load-bearing and creep-resistant properties after Cu addition.
The Cu-doped alloy will have higher effective thermal conductivity than the undoped HEA under 700–1000 °C thermal cycling.
The Cu-doped alloy will avoid a significant loss of elevated-temperature tensile strength or creep resistance relative to the undoped HEA.
Excessive Cu concentration or processing-induced phase separation may create deleterious microstructural features and reduce structural integrity.
A controlled comparison of nominally identical undoped and approximately 5 at% Cu-doped samples can test the proposed thermal and mechanical effects.

Failure to obtain at least an approximately 10% thermal-conductivity increase, or a greater than approximately 10% loss in tensile strength or creep resistance, is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
